Abstain

ab-STAYN -- the second syllable rhymes with 'rain'. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To abstain is to restrain oneself from doing or enjoying something.

The councilwoman chose to abstain from the vote because her family owned land near the proposed construction site.

Worked Example

Dessert is passed around the table, but the marathon runner politely waves it away, sticking to the strict diet she follows before every race.

Deliberately holding herself back from something tempting is exactly what it means to abstain. Unlike 'indulge,' which means giving in to a desire, to abstain means to refuse it on purpose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

refrain: to hold oneself back from doing something

forgo: to give something up or do without it

desist: to stop doing something, often formally or by order

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indulge: to give in to a desire or pleasure

partake: to take part in something or have a share of it

Where it sits · how firm and lasting the self-denial is — refrain → abstain → desist

refrain vs. abstain: Refrain is lighter and often more temporary than abstain -- you might refrain from talking during a movie, while to abstain suggests a firmer, more deliberate act of self-denial, often over a longer period.

desist vs. abstain: Desist can sound stronger and more official than abstain: to abstain is a personal choice to hold back, while desist often means stopping something already underway, sometimes because an authority demands it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — abs-

prefix — abs-: away, away from (Latin)

root — tain

root — tain: to hold (from Latin tenere; spelled -tain in English, as in retain and contain)

Put it together

Put it together: Abstain comes from Latin abs- ('away from') plus tenere ('to hold'), spelled -tain in English. To abstain is literally to hold yourself away from something -- you keep your own hands off the thing you are refusing.

Use the root in a new word: retain

Use the root in a new word: retain: Even after the merger, the company managed to retain most of its original employees.

Root Check

Word Choice

Abstain is almost always followed by 'from,' as in 'abstain from sweets' or 'abstain from arguing.' It is also the official word for choosing not to cast a vote at all -- a determined act of self-restraint rather than simple forgetfulness.
